# Modal

Universal modal component for creating dialog windows that overlay the main content. It is a real dialog on Base UI's `Dialog`, placed in `Blanket`: opening it moves focus inside and keeps it there, the page behind is hidden from assistive tech and stops scrolling, Escape and a press on the blanket close it, and closing returns focus to what had it. It takes a stack slot from the shared overlay module (`@/lib/overlay`) alongside `PatternDrawer`: at most two stack, a third stays closed and calls `onClose`. A follow-up about the dialog itself — "discard these edits?" — is best shown in place: the caller swaps `title`, `body` and the footer buttons, driven by its own state. A confirm raised as a second Modal is allowed too; it is the most that stacks.

Also asked as: confirm, confirmation dialog, destructive confirm, popup window, modal dialog.

**Import:** `import { Modal } from '@/components';`

## Usage

Use `Modal` when the next step has to happen before anything else can: a
destructive confirmation, a short form that would derail the page, a detail view
the person closes and returns from. It is the one messaging component that takes
focus from the page, so it fits when interrupting is the point.

The footer is built in: pass `primaryButton` and `secondaryButton` as objects and
the component renders the `Button` pair, aligned right. Pass `footer` for other
actions, such as a Delete on the left or a single primary. Opening a Modal
closes a floating Sidebar; a docked one stays.

### Width guidance

`width` takes a step of `MODAL_WIDTHS`: that
many columns of the screen grid plus the modal pad.

| Width | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| 6-col | A confirmation or a short question. 384 at 768, 512 at 1024, 640 from 1280. |
| 8-col | A short form. 507 at 768, 677 at 1024, 848 from 1280. |
| 10-col | A table or an editor. 629 at 768, 843 at 1024, 1056 from 1280. |

The width grows with the screen, never shrinks, and ignores the Sidebar. The
height hugs its content up to the cap the Blanket sets
(`--blanket-max-height-modal`); `height="fill"` sits at that cap.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the Modal with the action or decision: "Delete account?". | Use a vague title such as "Warning". |
| Say what happens and whether it can be undone. | Hide the consequence in the body. |
| Label buttons with verbs that match the title: "Delete", "Cancel". | Use "Yes" and "No". |

## Alternatives

- For a message the person only reads, use `SectionMessage` in the page or `Flag` at the screen corner.
- For a task that takes more than a screen or has sections, use `PageLayout` with `frame="focused"`.
- For a task that keeps the page in view, use `PatternDrawer`: a row's details, filters, a short edit.
- For a small aside anchored to a control, use `Popup`.
- For a list of actions or a value to pick, use `DropdownMenu` or `Select`.

## Best practices

### Size the Modal to its content with a step of `MODAL_WIDTHS`. {#size-the-modal-to-its-content-with-a-step-of-modalwidths}

A short confirmation takes `6-col`, a short form `8-col`, a table or an editor
`10-col`. A step grows with the screen; a fixed number keeps one size on every
screen.

Do: The narrowest step for a short question.
Don't: The widest step around one sentence.

### Keep Close on a Modal unless the person has to answer it. {#keep-close-on-a-modal-unless-the-person-has-to-answer-it}

An informational Modal keeps its close button; `showCloseButton={false}` is for
a decision that has to be answered from the footer.

Do: Close stays on an informational dialog.
Don't: No way out of an informational dialog.

### Add `dividers` when the Modal body scrolls. {#add-dividers-when-the-modal-body-scrolls}

The rules mark where the header and footer stay put while the body scrolls; a
short body reads cleaner without them.

Do: Dividers around a scrolling body.
Don't: Dividers around a short body.

### Give the Modal footer a button. {#give-the-modal-footer-a-button}

`showBottomButtons` defaults to true, and the footer renders only when
`primaryButton`, `secondaryButton` or `footer` is given; describe the actions as
objects and the component renders the Button pair.

### Show a follow-up decision in the same Modal, or stack its confirm as a second Modal. {#show-a-follow-up-decision-in-the-same-modal-or-stack-its-confirm-as-a-second-modal}

The confirm view swaps the same Modal's title, body and footer, and Back returns
to the form with what was typed. A confirm raised as a second Modal stacks over
the first: at most `MAX_STACKED_OVERLAYS` overlays
stack, a `PatternDrawer` counted among them, and one more stays closed and calls
its `onClose`.

```jsx
<Modal
  title={confirming ? 'Discard changes?' : 'Session settings'}
  show={open}
  onClose={close}
  secondaryButton={confirming ? { text: 'Back', onClick: () => setConfirming(false) } : { text: 'Cancel', onClick: close }}
  primaryButton={confirming ? { text: 'Discard changes', appearance: 'danger', onClick: discard } : { text: 'Save', onClick: save }}
>
  {confirming ? 'Your edits to this session are not saved.' : settingsForm}
</Modal>
```

## Accessibility

- **Escape and a press on the Blanket close the Modal by default.** `keyboard`
  and `backdrop` both default to `true`. Turning either off leaves the close
  button as the exit, so keep that button. The header, and its close button, is
  left out only when the Modal has no `title`, no `description`, no
  `headerActions` and `showBottomButtons` is false.
- **The close button is labeled `Close modal`**, hard-coded. Its icon is
  `aria-hidden`. `showCloseButton={false}` removes it; keep Escape or a footer
  action as a way out.
- **The title is the dialog's h1 and its accessible name**, through
  `aria-labelledby`: the dialog reads as its own page. The `description`
  describes it, through `aria-describedby`. A Modal with no title takes
  `ariaLabel`.
- **A body that scrolls is focusable.** Once the content runs past the cap, the
  body gets `tabIndex={0}` so a keyboard user can scroll it.
- **Loading is announced as busy.** `loading` sets `aria-busy` on the body while
  the skeleton bars stand in for it.
- **Opening traps focus inside the dialog and closing returns it to the
  trigger.** Tab cycles within the dialog; a view change (the confirm view
  swapping in) moves focus into the dialog again.
- **Turn off the Blanket click for an inline confirmation of a destructive
  action.** Set `backdrop="static"` (or `false`) while the confirmation shows,
  so a stray click outside cannot destroy something by accident; Close, Escape
  or the footer's Back still work.
- **Focus order is Close, then the content, then the secondary action, then
  the primary action.**
- **`renderAs="inline"` is for docs previews only.** It draws the panel with no
  Blanket, no focus trap and no Escape, so a live dialog keeps the default
  `renderAs="modal"`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the dialog panel. |
| `title` | string | — | The dialog's h1, and its accessible name. |
| `description` | node | — | A line under the title, read as the dialog's description. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | — | The dialog's accessible name when it has no visible `title`. |
| `body` | string or node | — | The main content of the dialog. A string is drawn as body text; a node is drawn as given. `children` is rendered after it. |
| `height` | enum | `'hug'` | `hug` grows with the content to the screen less 128 and then scrolls its body; `fill` sits at that cap. |
| `showBottomButtons` | bool | `true` | Show the footer: `footer`, or the secondary and primary buttons. |
| `showCloseButton` | bool | `true` | The header's close button. Off for a dialog that has to be answered. |
| `headerActions` | node | — | Icon buttons in the header, before the close button. |
| `footer` | node | — | Custom footer actions in place of the two buttons, aligned right. |
| `dividers` | bool | `false` | A rule under the header and over the footer. |
| `loading` | bool | `false` | Skeleton bars in place of the body while its content loads. |
| `show` | bool | `false` | Whether the dialog is open. Controlled by the parent: set it to false in `onClose` to close. |
| `backdrop` | enum | `true` | `true` (default): a click on the blanket closes. `static`: the blanket shows but refuses to close on a click. `false`: no close on a click. |
| `keyboard` | bool | `true` | Escape closes, by default. `false` for a dialog that has to be answered. |
| `renderAs` | enum | `'modal'` | `modal` (default) opens as a real dialog over the page; `inline` draws the same panel in place as a plain block, for docs previews. |
| `primaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The confirming footer button, drawn on the right. Takes `text` (default "Confirm"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `primary`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `secondaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The cancelling footer button, drawn left of the primary one. Takes `text` (default "Cancel"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `default`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `onClose` | func | — | Called when the dialog asks to close: the close button, Escape (unless `keyboard` is false) or a press on the blanket (unless `backdrop` blocks it). The parent sets `show` to false. |
| `width` | enum or number or string | `'6-col'` | `6-col` · `8-col` · `10-col`: 6 · 8 · 10 columns of the screen grid plus the modal pad. Grows with the screen, never shrinks, ignores the sidebar. A number or a length is a fixed width, kept for the callers that still pass one. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the dialog panel beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the dialog panel. A fixed `width` is applied after them. |
| `children` | node | — | More content rendered in the body after `body`, for composing the dialog contents directly. |

## Variants

**`height`** — `hug` · `fill`

**`backdrop`** — `static`

**`renderAs`** — `modal` · `inline`

Anything not listed is not a valid value.

## Related

- `PatternModal`: use when a docs page or a mockup draws the Modal shell inline, with no focus trap.
- `Blanket`: use when a new blocking layer needs the dimmed screen under it; `Modal` brings its own.
- `PageLayout`: use when choosing between a Modal and a focused page; its Focused frame section weighs the two.
